rootCause: The repository bundles an ancient copy of `xonsh` (last updated ~2017) that imports `ast.Num`, `ast.Str`, `ast.Bytes`, `ast.Ellipsis` – all removed from Python's `ast` module in 3.12+. The `setup.py` builds this vendored `xonsh` during `pip install gitsome`, so the build fails on Python 3.14. The README still claims support only up to Python 3.7 and gives no guidance for modern Ubuntu (24.04+/26.04) where the system Python is ≥3.12.

--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -485,6 +485,34 @@ For most linux users, `pip3` can be installed on your system using the `python3
 See this [ticket](https://github.com/donnemartin/gitsome/issues/4) for more details.
 
 ### Virtual Environment Installation
+#### Ubuntu 24.04 / 26.04 (Python 3.12+) – Required Workaround
+The bundled `xonsh` is incompatible with Python ≥3.12. You must install an older Python (3.11 or 3.10) from the deadsnakes PPA and create a virtual environment with it.
+
+    $ sudo apt-get update
+    $ sudo apt-get install -y software-properties-common
+    $ sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:deadsnakes/ppa
+    $ sudo apt-get update
+    $ sudo apt-get install -y python3.11 python3.11-venv python3.11-dev
+    $ python3.11 -m venv ~/venv-gitsome
+    $ source ~/venv-gitsome/bin/activate
+    $ pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
+    $ pip install gitsome
+
+After activation, the `gh` and `gitsome` commands will be available. To persist the environment, add `source ~/venv-gitsome/bin/activate` to your shell profile.
+
+If you prefer Python 3.10, replace `python3.11` with `python3.10` in the commands above.

rootCause: The `gitsome` package depends on `feedparser==5.2.1` which uses `distutils` (removed in setuptools≥60). The verify script pins `setuptools<81` but gets 75.3.4 which lacks `distutils`, causing `feedparser`'s `setup.py` to fail with "use_2to3 is invalid". The fix is to pin `setuptools<60` (last version with `distutils`) during installation.
